quests.instruction: Which usually carries travellers fastest across 1,500 kilometres of land?
quests.hint: It travels high above the ground, where nothing slows it down.
quests.explanation: Airplanes fly much faster than trains or buses, so long journeys take hours instead of days. Time at the airport counts too.
quests.funFact: Cruising airliners fly at about 900 kilometres per hour.

quests.instruction: Which of these is the slowest way to cover 10 kilometres?
quests.hint: It has no wheels at all.
quests.explanation: Walking is about five kilometres per hour, so ten kilometres takes around two hours. Bicycles and buses are much faster.
quests.funFact: Walking is one of the healthiest ways to travel because it gets your whole body moving.

quests.instruction: Which of these can travel the fastest of all?
quests.hint: It has to go fast enough to escape Earth's pull.
quests.explanation: A rocket reaches thousands of kilometres per hour, which is far faster than any train or airplane.
quests.funFact: The International Space Station circles Earth about every 90 minutes.

quests.instruction: Which can carry the most passengers in a single trip?
quests.hint: It has many carriages joined together in a line.
quests.explanation: A train can have many carriages, each with lots of seats, so it carries far more people than a bus or a car.
quests.funFact: Some metro trains have open carriages from end to end so more people can fit inside.

quests.instruction: Which of these is the smallest vehicle that can carry a person?
quests.hint: You stand on it and it fits in a cupboard.
quests.explanation: A kick scooter is tiny and light. It is easy to store, but it only carries one rider.
quests.funFact: Kick scooters can be stored under a desk or in a cupboard.

quests.instruction: Which of these weighs the most?
quests.hint: It carries thousands of tonnes of cargo.
quests.explanation: Big ships weigh tens of thousands of tonnes, far more than any truck or car.
quests.funFact: A large container ship can weigh more than 100,000 tonnes when it is fully loaded.

quests.instruction: Which can leave whenever you want and take you straight to your own front door?
quests.hint: It does not follow a timetable or a fixed route.
quests.explanation: A private car does not follow a timetable. That freedom is useful, but it also adds traffic and needs a parking space.
quests.funFact: Cars are often parked for most of the day.

quests.instruction: Which of these has no choice but to follow its tracks?
quests.hint: Its wheels stay on metal rails.
quests.explanation: A train follows fixed rails, so it cannot swerve or change direction. That makes it safe on its own track, but less flexible than road vehicles.
quests.funFact: Railway signals work like traffic lights to keep trains a safe distance apart.

quests.instruction: Which can you use any time, without waiting for a timetable?
quests.hint: It is always ready when you are.
quests.explanation: A bicycle is ready whenever you are. Buses and trains need you to fit in with their schedule.
quests.funFact: In some cities, shared bicycles can be borrowed from docking stations at any time.

quests.instruction: Which costs the least to run each week?
quests.hint: It needs no fuel, only some air in the tyres.
quests.explanation: A bicycle needs no fuel and very little repair. Engines cost money to fill up and fix.
quests.funFact: Bicycles need only a little oil for the chain and air in the tyres.

quests.instruction: Which uses the most fuel in one hour of travel?
quests.hint: It has huge jet engines.
quests.explanation: Planes burn lots of fuel to stay in the air and carry heavy loads. They also carry hundreds of passengers at once.
quests.funFact: A large airliner can burn thousands of litres of fuel every hour.

quests.instruction: On a heavy rainy day, which keeps passengers dry and comfortable?
quests.hint: It has a roof, windows, and doors.
quests.explanation: Cars have roofs and windows that keep out rain. Bikes and scooters leave riders exposed, so they need raincoats.
quests.funFact: Many cars have heaters and air conditioning to keep passengers comfortable in any weather.

quests.instruction: Which boat is the quietest because it uses no engine?
quests.hint: It moves with the wind instead.
quests.explanation: A sailboat moves with the wind, so there is no engine noise. Many sailors enjoy the peaceful sound of the water.
quests.funFact: Many sailboats also carry a small engine for entering harbours or sailing on calm days.

quests.instruction: Which can travel in very shallow water where big boats would get stuck?
quests.hint: It sits high in the water and weighs very little.
quests.explanation: A canoe sits high in the water, so it can pass over shallow places. Big ships need deep water.
quests.funFact: Canoes can be carried by two people from one river to another.

quests.instruction: Which is slower than a plane but lets passengers stroll on deck and watch the sea for days?
quests.hint: Think of a floating holiday.
quests.explanation: A cruise ship travels slowly, but the journey is part of the holiday. Passengers can walk around, swim, and enjoy the views.
quests.funFact: Some cruise ships have theatres, swimming pools, and even ice rinks.

quests.instruction: Which train usually stops every few minutes at stations close together inside a city?
quests.hint: It is designed for short hops across town.
quests.explanation: Metro trains are designed for short hops across a city, so stations are close together. They speed up and stop quickly.
quests.funFact: Some metro systems run trains every two or three minutes at busy times.

quests.instruction: Which train is built for travelling quickly between faraway cities, with few stops?
quests.hint: It has a sleek nose and travels on its own special track.
quests.explanation: A high-speed train travels long distances quickly and stops only at big stations. That is the opposite of a city metro.
quests.funFact: High-speed railways are built almost straight, because fast trains cannot take sharp curves.

quests.instruction: Which needs expensive rails built into the street, so its route is hard to change?
quests.hint: Its path is set into the road itself.
quests.explanation: A tram follows rails laid into the road. Changing a route means building new track, while buses can use any road.
quests.funFact: Several cities have opened new tram lines in recent years.

quests.instruction: Which needs the longest strip of ground to take off?
quests.hint: It is heavy and must build up a lot of speed.
quests.explanation: A big airliner is heavy and needs a long runway to reach take-off speed. A helicopter lifts straight up.
quests.funFact: Some airports have runways more than three kilometres long.

quests.instruction: Which is the loudest at take-off?
quests.hint: It makes a huge roar and leaves a trail of fire.
quests.explanation: Rocket engines produce an enormous roar. Launch sites are kept far from people.
quests.funFact: Launch pads spray huge amounts of water to soften the noise.

quests.instruction: Which can hover in one spot but cannot fly as fast or as far as an airplane?
quests.hint: Spinning blades hold it in the air.
quests.explanation: A helicopter's spinning blades let it stay in one place, but this makes it slower and shorter-ranged than a plane.
quests.funFact: A helicopter's tail rotor keeps its body from spinning around.

quests.instruction: On a long uphill road, which needs the most effort from the rider's own legs?
quests.hint: Its only engine is the person riding it.
quests.explanation: A bicycle has no motor, so riders do all the work going uphill. Gears make hills easier by spreading out the effort.
quests.funFact: Electric bicycles have a small motor that helps riders on hills.

quests.instruction: Which is best for a fast journey on an open highway?
quests.hint: It has an engine strong enough to keep up with traffic.
quests.explanation: A motorcycle's engine can reach highway speeds. Bicycles and kick scooters are not built for high-speed roads.
quests.funFact: Motorcycle riders wear helmets and protective clothing because they have less protection than car drivers.

quests.instruction: On a busy road, which of these is smallest and easiest for a truck driver to overlook?
quests.hint: Think about which one could hide in a blind spot.
quests.explanation: Small, narrow vehicles can hide in blind spots, so riders need lights and bright clothes to stand out. Drivers should check carefully.
quests.funFact: Many trucks carry a sign saying that if you cannot see the mirrors, the driver cannot see you.

quests.instruction: Which can lift heavy things high into the air that a truck cannot?
quests.hint: It has a tall arm and a hook.
quests.explanation: A crane can lift heavy loads high above the ground. A truck can carry things, but cannot raise them up to a tall building.
quests.funFact: Cranes use heavy weights at the back to stay balanced when they lift.

quests.instruction: Which of these needs food and rest instead of fuel?
quests.hint: It is a living thing, not a machine.
quests.explanation: A horse is powered by food and water, not fuel. It needs rest, care, and time to recover after work.
quests.funFact: A healthy horse can walk for hours but needs frequent rests and water.

quests.instruction: Which can pull heavy machines across soft, muddy ground that would trap a sports car?
quests.hint: Look for big tyres and a very strong engine.
quests.explanation: A tractor has huge tyres and a powerful engine. They spread its weight and grip soft ground where a sports car would get stuck.
quests.funFact: Some tractors have tracks like a bulldozer instead of wheels.

quests.instruction: Two friends live 3 kilometres apart. Which is the quickest, cheapest way for one to visit the other?
quests.hint: It is a short trip, so a small, cheap vehicle is best.
quests.explanation: For short trips, a bicycle is quick, costs very little, and needs no parking fee. Planes and taxis are too much for such a short trip.
quests.funFact: For short trips in busy cities, a bicycle can be as quick as a car.

quests.instruction: A traveller wants to go 600 kilometres between two cities quickly without driving. Which is the best choice?
quests.hint: Think of a vehicle that is fast and lets you relax along the way.
quests.explanation: A high-speed train covers long distances quickly and lets passengers relax. A bus takes much longer and a bicycle would take days.
quests.funFact: Many high-speed trains run from city centre to city centre, which saves time getting to and from airports.

quests.instruction: A museum visit in a crowded city centre has very little parking. Which choice avoids the parking problem?
quests.hint: It travels underneath the traffic and has its own stations.
quests.explanation: A metro train takes you close to the centre without needing a parking space. It also skips road jams.
quests.funFact: Cities with good metro systems often have less traffic on the roads.
